hook: Hyderabad's average home now costs *₹2.15 crore*, up ₹21 lakh in a year
hook_b: Hyderabad's average home now costs *₹2.15 crore*, up ₹21 lakh in a year
tldr: CRE Matrix-CREDAI data shows Hyderabad property prices rose 10.5% between Q3 2025 and Q3 2026, making it India's second-most expensive metro housing market after Delhi.

beats.what: Average property value rose from ₹1.94 crore to ₹2.15 crore. Only Chennai saw a bigger jump (₹25 lakh); Bengaluru was third (₹19 lakh).
beats.why: Industry players point to land costs and Hyderabad's no-cap FSI rule, which has pushed average flat size to around 2,000 sft vs 1,000-1,500 sft in Mumbai and Bengaluru.
beats.care: Bigger flats mean bigger ticket sizes, so first-time buyers face a higher entry price even as demand cools.
